title: Environmental Print Walk
strapline: Reading the world before you can read a book — the logos, signs and words that are everywhere.
intent: Children discover that print is everywhere and carries meaning — signs, labels, logos, names all say something.
Children begin to 'read' familiar print in context, an early and confidence-building step into reading.
Children notice letters and words in the real world, linking them to the sounds and names they know.
Children build the understanding that print is all around and useful, motivating them to want to read.
Children develop looking, noticing and talking as they hunt for and discuss the print they find.
implementation: Take a 'print walk' around the setting, garden or local street, spotting signs, labels and familiar logos.
Point out and read print in context: the exit sign, the road name, the shop logo, the cereal box.
Photograph the print children spot and make a class book or display of 'print we found'.
Bring in packaging and logos from home the children recognise — the print they can already 'read'.
Talk about what print is for: 'this word tells cars to stop', 'this label says what's inside'.
Draw attention to letters children know: 'that's a P — like in your name, Priya!'.
Set up a role-play shop or street with the environmental print children have collected.
key_questions: What do you think that sign says?
How did you know what it said?
Can you spot any letters you know?
What is this print for — what is it telling us?
Where else have you seen this word or logo?

impact.text: Children notice print in the environment and know it carries meaning.
Children 'read' familiar logos and signs in context.
Children spot and name letters they recognise in the world.
Children talk about what different print is for.
Children want to find and share print, showing motivation to read.
Children look closely and notice detail in their surroundings.

enhancements: A collection of familiar packaging and logos for a sorting and role-play shop.
A photo book of 'print in our world' made from the children's finds.
Clipboards and cameras for children to record the print they spot.
Labels around the room at child height naming everyday things.
A local walk to the shops, park and post box to hunt for signs.
A road-sign small world or floor mat with printed signs to read.

playing_exploring: Children hunt for print with curiosity, spotting it everywhere.
They bring in and share print they recognise from home.
active_learning: Children keep looking, delighted each time they can 'read' a sign.
Recognising a logo builds the confidence to look for more.
creating_thinking: Children work out what print says from its shape and context.
They connect print in the world to letters and sounds they know.
